data_quality_checks: Both issuer actual quarters end September26,2026; matching dates do not make business models identical.
Both main vendor prices are November4 US closes; Intel vendor58.27 differs by one cent from frozen thesis58.28. Keep distinction explicit; do not silently change frozen model.
2028 Intel12.969B netincome/2.418EPS implies5.36352B shares; AMD34.913/20.95 implies1.66649B. Plausible arithmetic, but not proof of matched GAAP adjustments.
MarketScreener AMD2026/2027 EBIT14.221/31.369B exceeds EBITDA13.914/30.402B, indicating mixed or inconsistent series. Exclude its EV/EBITDA and EV/EBIT from a purportedly matched valuation.

recommended_pitch_exhibit.interpretation: The screen raises the question of what cash returns Intel must earn to justify near-parity with AMD. Current-quarter cash results do not prove Intel converts worse: its CFO-minus-capex margin was slightly higher. The outright/relative short still needs durable return evidence.

verdict.fills_gap: Provides a reproducible, dated peer screen and primary-source capital-intensity check, plus a transparent valuation sensitivity. It does not deliver a fully reconciled economic peer valuation or a new fair-value target.
verdict.effect_on_short: Mixed. Intel2028vendorP/E is only about3% aboveAMD, so simple equal-multiple repricing offers little support for a large short payoff. Higher direct capital intensity supports investigating durable cash returns, but AMD also had weak current cash conversion. Our own4.17EPSproxy implies onlyabout14x atentry, so our centralDCF46.96 requires a lower~11.27x of that sameproxy; peer screen does not independently validate that discount.
verdict.sotp_rejected: No independentSOTPtarget: assigning AMD multiple to Products and TSMC multiple to internal Foundry would risk double-counting internal manufacturing earnings and ignores transferpricing, minoritycapital, corporateexpense and replacementcapex.
